instruction: Reduce my desktop volume to 10 percent.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command:
pulseaudio --start
pactl list sinks | grep '^[[:space:]]Volume:' | head -n 1 | awk '{print $5}' | sed 's/%//g'

metadata.explanation: Task requires reducing the system volume to 10%. Evaluator uses existing exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter to check PulseAudio volume is '10\n'. No custom functions needed - reusing official evaluator components.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses vm_command_line getter to execute PulseAudio volume check command
Metric exact_match appropriately compares the command output against expected value '10\n'
Expected value '10\n' correctly represents 10% volume with newline from command output
Complete coverage: single requirement (volume = 10%) is verified
Minor risk: Command uses 'awk {print $5}' which assumes volume percentage is in 5th field - this may be fragile across different PulseAudio output formats or audio configurations
The command chain (pactl list sinks | grep Volume | awk) could fail if volume format differs (e.g., stereo vs mono, different locales)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using a more robust extraction method, such as: pactl list sinks | grep -Po '\d+(?=%)' | head -n 1 to extract percentage directly via regex
Alternative: Use pactl get-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ for more reliable output format
Consider adding tolerance for whitespace variations in expected value comparison
